arms.goal: Single-lever (architecture parity) re-run of the collapsed 160M arm. Questions: survive step 4000? beat 70M frozen 1.4692?
arms.note: VERDICT 2026-09-23 15:00: fix CONFIRMED as crash-cure — clean train descent to 2.875, no eval nulls, no plateau, guard fired properly. But capacity answer is NO: best 1.5890 @2100 (~69M tok), early-stop at 4700 (val 1.8546 > best+15% while TRAIN still falling = classic overfit-at-hot-LR mid-schedule, NOT a collapse). 160M still loses to 70M champion 1.4699@12000. Pattern across all three 50k long arms: val bottoms at 130-2400 steps then climbs while train descends; the 70M's improvement lived in its ANNEALING phase (lr decay after step ~7000) — neither 160M arm ever got there before the guard aborted it. Next hypothesis: schedule-length, not size. Collision note (attempt 1/1312) kept below.

CAVEAT ON TRANSFER: the auto-diff shows the ONLY arg changes vs p50k-lr-15e-4 are dropout 0.1 and rotary_pct 1.0 - corpus, eff_batch, lr and vocab are all UNCHANGED, so this is a schedule-length extension, not a corpus/lr comparison. ignore_dirs_note: 2026-09-29: unregistered dirs were classified, not blanket-ignored. Real evidence runs (m66m-4p5gb-40k, pythia-owt50kv2-lr-15e-4-long, pile-native-tok-200step) were registered as arms; the rest are calibration smokes (batch sweep for tok/s, 3-step ladder build checks, short 4k-vocab probes) plus one launch casualty. Calibration runs answer 'does it fit and how fast', not 'what did the model learn', so they carry no verdict and are ignored by name.
